CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

STATUSLINE SETUP NEEDED: The caveman plugin includes a statusline badge showing active mode (e.g. [CAVEMAN], [CAVEMAN:ULTRA]). It is not configured yet. To enable, add this to /home/symphony/.claude/settings.json: "statusLine": { "type": "command", "command": "bash \"/home/symphony/.claude/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/84cc3c14fa1e/hooks/caveman-statusline.sh\"" } Proactively offer to set this up for the user on first interaction.

<EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>
You have superpowers.

**Below is the full content of your 'superpowers:using-superpowers' skill - your introduction to using skills. For all other skills, use the 'Skill' tool:**

---
name: using-superpowers
description: Use when starting any conversation - establishes how to find and use skills, requiring Skill tool invocation before ANY response including clarifying questions
---

<SUBAGENT-STOP>
If you were dispatched as a subagent to execute a specific task, skip this skill.
</SUBAGENT-STOP>

<EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>
If you think there is even a 1% chance a skill might apply to what you are doing, you ABSOLUTELY MUST invoke the skill.

IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.

This is not negotiable. This is not optional. You cannot rationalize your way out of this.
</EXTREMELY-IMPORTANT>

## Instruction Priority

Superpowers skills override default system prompt behavior, but **user instructions always take precedence**:

1. **User's explicit instructions** (CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, AGENTS.md, direct requests) — highest priority
2. **Superpowers skills** — override default system behavior where they conflict
3. **Default system prompt** — lowest priority

If CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, or AGENTS.md says "don't use TDD" and a skill says "always use TDD," follow the user's instructions. The user is in control.

## How to Access Skills

**In Claude Code:** Use the `Skill` tool. When you invoke a skill, its content is loaded and presented to you—follow it directly. Never use the Read tool on skill files.

**In Copilot CLI:** Use the `skill` tool. Skills are auto-discovered from installed plugins. The `skill` tool works the same as Claude Code's `Skill` tool.

**In Gemini CLI:** Skills activate via the `activate_skill` tool. Gemini loads skill metadata at session start and activates the full content on demand.

**In other environments:** Check your platform's documentation for how skills are loaded.

## Platform Adaptation

Skills use Claude Code tool names. Non-CC platforms: see `references/copilot-tools.md` (Copilot CLI), `references/codex-tools.md` (Codex) for tool equivalents. Gemini CLI users get the tool mapping loaded automatically via GEMINI.md.

# Using Skills

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action.** Even a 1% chance a skill might apply means that you should invoke the skill to check. If an invoked skill turns out to be wrong for the situation, you don't need to use it.

```dot
digraph skill_flow {
    "User message received" [shape=doublecircle];
    "About to EnterPlanMode?" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Already brainstormed?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke brainstorming skill" [shape=box];
    "Might any skill apply?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke Skill tool" [shape=box];
    "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'" [shape=box];
    "Has checklist?" [shape=diamond];
    "Create TodoWrite todo per item" [shape=box];
    "Follow skill exactly" [shape=box];
    "Respond (including clarifications)" [shape=doublecircle];

    "About to EnterPlanMode?" -> "Already brainstormed?";
    "Already brainstormed?" -> "Invoke brainstorming skill" [label="no"];
    "Already brainstormed?" -> "Might any skill apply?" [label="yes"];
    "Invoke brainstorming skill" -> "Might any skill apply?";

    "User message received" -> "Might any skill apply?";
    "Might any skill apply?" -> "Invoke Skill tool" [label="yes, even 1%"];
    "Might any skill apply?" -> "Respond (including clarifications)" [label="definitely not"];
    "Invoke Skill tool" -> "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'";
    "Announce: 'Using [skill] to [purpose]'" -> "Has checklist?";
    "Has checklist?" -> "Create TodoWrite todo per item" [label="yes"];
    "Has checklist?" -> "Follow skill exactly" [label="no"];
    "Create TodoWrite todo per item" -> "Follow skill exactly";
}
```

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills could apply, use this order:

1. **Process skills first** (brainstorming, debugging) - these determine HOW to approach the task
2. **Implementation skills second** (frontend-design, mcp-builder) - these guide execution

"Let's build X" → brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
"Fix this bug" → debugging first, then domain-specific skills.

## Skill Types

**Rigid** (TDD, debugging): Follow exactly. Don't adapt away discipline.

**Flexible** (patterns): Adapt principles to context.

The skill itself tells you which.

## User Instructions

Instructions say WHAT, not HOW. "Add X" or "Fix Y" doesn't mean skip workflows.


</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>

class ThemeModeController extends StateNotifier<ThemeMode> {
  static const _key = 'theme_mode';
  
  Future<void> _hydrate() async {
    final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
    switch (prefs.getString(_key)) {
      case 'dark': state = ThemeMode.dark; break;
      case 'light': state = ThemeMode.light; break;
      case 'system': state = ThemeMode.system; break;
    }
  }

}

# Implementation Plan: APP-LOCK for CSC291-DroneAid

## Summary

App-lock layers a device-local PIN/biometric gate *on top of* the existing Firebase National-ID login. After a Firebase session exists, an enabled user must unlock with a PIN (baseline) or fingerprint (optional) before app content is revealed. The lock secret never touches Firestore. The gate is implemented as a **widget overlay** in the existing `MaterialApp.router` `builder` (not a router redirect), the lock state lives in a non-autoDispose `LockController extends StateNotifier<LockState>`, lifecycle detection lives inside that controller via `AppLifecycleListener`, and the secret is a salted SHA-256 hash in `flutter_secure_storage` keyed per-uid.

---

## 1. Lock-state management

### Provider shape

A four-value state (NOT three) so the gate never flashes content or a lock screen before hydration resolves:

```dart
enum LockState { unknown, disabled, locked, unlocked }
```

- `unknown` — pre-hydration; gate renders `AuthSplash`.
- `disabled` — user has no PIN enabled; gate renders child (behaves exactly as today).
- `locked` — enabled and not yet unlocked this session/grace; gate renders `LockScreen`.
- `unlocked` — verified; gate renders child.

`LockController extends StateNotifier<LockState>`, constructed at `unknown`, exposed via a plain (non-autoDispose, non-family) provider so it persists for the whole app lifetime:

```dart
final lockControllerProvider =
    StateNotifierProvider<LockController, LockState>((ref) => LockController(ref));
```

Responsibilities (composes a `LockRepository` for storage; see file list):
- `_hydrate()` in constructor: read `enabled` flag + whether a PIN hash exists for the current uid. If signed-out or not enabled → `disabled`. If enabled → `locked` (cold start always locks unconditionally — grace only applies to resume, section 3).
- `ref.listen(authStateProvider, ...)`: on **uid change**, re-hydrate. On **sign-out** (`user == null`) → `disabled`. This is what makes the lock *per-uid* and resolves edge cases (section 6).
- `Future<bool> verifyPin(String pin)` → compares salted hash; on success `state = unlocked`.
- `Future<bool> verifyBiometric()` → `local_auth`; on success `state = unlocked`.
- `void lockNow()` → if enabled, `state = locked` ("Lock now" affordance).
- Settings mutators (called only from the profile Security section): `setPin`, `changePin`, `removePin`, `setBiometricEnabled` — these update storage and recompute `state` (e.g. setting a PIN from `disabled` leaves the app `unlocked` for the current session; removing a PIN → `disabled`).

### Hydration ("is app-lock enabled? is a PIN set?")

The controller asks `LockRepository`, which keys all reads/writes by the **current uid** (read once from `FirebaseAuth.instance.currentUser?.uid`, also refreshed via the `authStateProvider` listen):
- `lock_enabled:<uid>` (bool, SharedPreferences) — the toggle.
- `lock_biometric:<uid>` (bool, SharedPreferences) — biometric-additive flag.
- `lock_pin:<uid>` (string, **flutter_secure_storage**) — `"<saltHex>:<sha256(salt+pin)Hex>"`.

Booleans in SharedPreferences (mirrors `theme_mode_provider`'s pattern); the secret in Keystore-backed secure storage. Per-uid keying keeps it device-local (req 1) while namespacing per account.

---

## 2. Gate mechanism — RECOMMENDATION: (b) Widget overlay (`LockGate`)

**Recommended decisively: (b).** Reasoning, grounded in this codebase:

1. **An identical seam already exists.** `main.dart:92-96` — `MaterialApp.router`'s `builder` already does `if (auth.isLoading) return const AuthSplash(); return child;`. The lock gate is one more branch in a *proven* insertion point that already renders a full `Scaffold` (`AuthSplash`) over the router. Approach (a) has no comparable existing seam.

2. **The router stays completely untouched** (`router.dart` is not modified). Approach (a) would thread lock state into the *already-dense* `redirect` (which juggles `auth.isLoading`, `profile.isLoading`, `_publicRoutes`, landing computation, and the admin guard at lines 42-65) plus extend `_AuthListenable` to watch a third provider. Ordering-sensitive and bug-prone.

3. **Deep links / intended location are preserved for free.** With (b) the router resolves the real destination (`/user/tracking/:flightId`, `/admin/requests/:reqId`, etc.) *underneath* the overlay; the instant `state` flips to `unlocked` the gate returns `child` and the correct page is already there — zero bookkeeping. With (a), `/lock` replaces the location, so on unlock you must stash `state.matchedLocation` and restore it manually, and handle every deep-link path yourself.

4. **Back-button safety.** In (a), `/lock` is a real route the Android back button can pop, bypassing the lock — you'd patch it with `PopScope`. In (b) the overlay is not a route, so back-button traversal doesn't apply (still wrap the lock screen in `PopScope(canPop: false)` defensively).

5. **Role-agnostic.** The overlay sits above both `UserShell` and `AdminShell` and the public routes uniformly — no admin/user special-casing, unlike the per-prefix logic a redirect would need.

6. **AuthSplash interaction is clean.** The gate's `unknown` branch reuses `AuthSplash`, so hydration looks identical to the existing auth-loading splash; no new loading-state coordination with the router.

### Gate builder ordering (critical — auth checked before lock)

The new `builder` (replacing `main.dart:92-96`), order matters to avoid showing a lock over `/login`:

```
final auth = ref.watch(authStateProvider);
final lock = ref.watch(lockControllerProvider);
if (auth.isLoading) return const AuthSplash();          // cold-start auth resolving
final user = auth.valueOrNull;
if (user == null) return child;                          // signed out → router shows /login
if (lock == LockState.unknown) return const AuthSplash(); // lock hydrating
if (lock == LockState.locked) return const LockScreen();  // gate
return child;                                             // disabled or unlocked
```

The per-uid sign-out reset (section 1) is the belt; this signed-out short-circuit is the suspenders.

---

## 3. Lifecycle observer (background→foreground + grace period)

**Use `AppLifecycleListener`** (Flutter 3.13+; the repo is `flutter >=3.22.0`, confirmed in `pubspec.yaml`). It is preferred over `WidgetsBindingObserver` because it exposes discrete `onPause`/`onHide`/`onResume` callbacks and needs no `BuildContext` — so it lives cleanly **inside `LockController`**.

- Construct an `AppLifecycleListener` in the controller's constructor; dispose it in `dispose()`.
- `onPause` / `onHide`: record `_backgroundedAt = DateTime.now()` (wall clock is fine per the task note). Only meaningful when `state` is `unlocked`.
- `onResume`: if app-lock is enabled and `state == unlocked`, compute `elapsed = DateTime.now().difference(_backgroundedAt)`. If `elapsed >= graceWindow` (const `Duration(seconds: 30)`) → `state = locked`. If under grace, do nothing (quick app-switches don't nag). If `_backgroundedAt == null` (e.g. resume with no recorded pause) → lock to be safe.

**Registration:** the controller is a non-autoDispose provider; instantiate it at startup by adding one line to `DroneAidApp.build` — `ref.watch(lockControllerProvider)` — exactly alongside the existing `ref.watch(fcmRegistrationProvider)` and `ref.watch(devTickRunnerProvider)` lines (`main.dart:73,77`). This is the established pattern for "keep this provider alive app-wide."

After a Firebase session exists, an enabled user must unlock with a PIN (baseline) or fingerprint (optional) before app content is revealed. The lock secret never touches Firestore. The gate is implemented as a **widget overlay** in the existing `MaterialApp.router` `builder` (not a router redirect), the lock state lives in a non-autoDispose `LockController extends StateNotifier<LockState>`, lifecycle detection lives inside that controller via `AppLifecycleListener`, and the secret is a salted SHA-256 hash in `flutter_secure_storage` keyed per-uid.

---

## 1. Lock-state management

### Provider shape

A four-value state (NOT three) so the gate never flashes content or a lock screen before hydration resolves:

```dart
enum LockState { unknown, disabled, locked, unlocked }
```

- `unknown` — pre-hydration; gate renders `AuthSplash`.
- `disabled` — user has no PIN enabled; gate renders child (behaves exactly as today).
- `locked` — enabled and not yet unlocked this session/grace; gate renders `LockScreen`.
- `unlocked` — verified; gate renders child.

`LockController extends StateNotifier<LockState>`, constructed at `unknown`, exposed via a plain (non-autoDispose, non-family) provider so it persists for the whole app lifetime:

```dart
final lockControllerProvider =
    StateNotifierProvider<LockController, LockState>((ref) => LockController(ref));
```

Responsibilities (composes a `LockRepository` for storage; see file list):
- `_hydrate()` in constructor: read `enabled` flag + whether a PIN hash exists for the current uid. If signed-out or not enabled → `disabled`. If enabled → `locked` (cold start always locks unconditionally — grace only applies to resume, section 3).
- `ref.listen(authStateProvider, ...)`: on **uid change**, re-hydrate. On **sign-out** (`user == null`) → `disabled`. This is what makes the lock *per-uid* and resolves edge cases (section 6).
- `Future<bool> verifyPin(String pin)` → compares salted hash; on success `state = unlocked`.
- `Future<bool> verifyBiometric()` → `local_auth`; on success `state = unlocked`.
- `void lockNow()` → if enabled, `state = locked` ("Lock now" affordance).
- Settings mutators (called only from the profile Security section): `setPin`, `changePin`, `removePin`, `setBiometricEnabled` — these update storage and recompute `state` (e.g. setting a PIN from `disabled` leaves the app `unlocked` for the current session; removing a PIN → `disabled`).

### Hydration ("is app-lock enabled? is a PIN set?")

The controller asks `LockRepository`, which keys all reads/writes by the **current uid** (read once from `FirebaseAuth.instance.currentUser?.uid`, also refreshed via the `authStateProvider` listen):
- `lock_enabled:<uid>` (bool, SharedPreferences) — the toggle.
- `lock_biometric:<uid>` (bool, SharedPreferences) — biometric-additive flag.
- `lock_pin:<uid>` (string, **flutter_secure_storage**) — `"<saltHex>:<sha256(salt+pin)Hex>"`.

Booleans in SharedPreferences (mirrors `theme_mode_provider`'s pattern); the secret in Keystore-backed secure storage. Per-uid keying keeps it device-local (req 1) while namespacing per account.

## 2. PIN cryptography design

**Honest framing (must appear in code docs):** a 4–6 digit PIN has only 10⁴–10⁶ entropy. PBKDF2 does **not** make it offline-brute-force-proof. The *primary* defenses are (a) Keystore-backed secure storage protecting the hash at rest, and (b) lockout/backoff limiting online guesses. PBKDF2 is defense-in-depth (slows an attacker who already extracted the hash). Do not describe SHA-256-or-PBKDF2 as "secure" without this context.

**Algorithm:** PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256.
- **Salt:** 16 bytes from a CSPRNG (`Random.secure()`), unique per PIN set.
- **Iterations:** `100000` in production; **injectable** so the unit suite can run with e.g. `1000` (100k × the test matrix would crawl).
- **Derived key length:** 32 bytes.
- **Stored fields** (all in secure storage, see §3):
  - `pin_salt` — base64 of the 16-byte salt
  - `pin_hash` — base64 of the 32-byte derived key
  - `pin_algo_version` — integer, currently `1` (lets a future migration re-hash transparently)
  - `pin_iterations` — integer (store the count actually used, so verify reproduces it even if the default changes)
- **Verify:** re-derive with stored salt + iterations, compare in **constant time** (fixed-length byte XOR-accumulate; never `==` on the strings, never early-return on first mismatch).
- **Salt uniqueness:** two consecutive `setPin` calls with the same PIN must yield different salts and different hashes (a unit test asserts this).

**Lockout / backoff:**
- Counter `failed_attempts` and `lockout_until` (epoch millis) live in **secure storage** so they survive an app restart — otherwise lockout is trivially bypassed by force-killing the app.
- Policy: after **5** consecutive failures, lock for a backoff window (e.g. 30s, then escalate: 30s → 1m → 5m). On a correct PIN, reset `failed_attempts` to 0 and clear `lockout_until`.
- `verifyPin` consults `lockout_until` first and returns a "locked-out, retry-after" result without even hashing when inside the window.

**`PinService` / `AppLockStore` API (signatures only — no implementation):**

```
// AppLockStore — thin async wrapper over the storage backend (the testable seam).
abstract class AppLockStore {
  Future<String?> read(String key);
  Future<void> write(String key, String value);
  Future<void> delete(String key);
  Future<void> deleteAll();
}

// PinService — pure-ish crypto + policy over an AppLockStore.
class PinService {
  PinService(this._store, {int iterations = 100000, Random? random});

  Future<bool>   hasPin();
  Future<void>   setPin(String pin);                 // generates salt, hashes, persists, resets counters
  Future<PinVerifyResult> verifyPin(String pin);     // checks lockout, hashes, constant-time compares, updates counters
  Future<void>   clearPin();                          // wipes pin_* + counters (used on disable / optional sign-out)

  Future<bool>   isAppLockEnabled();
  Future<void>   setAppLockEnabled(bool enabled);
  Future<bool>   isBiometricEnabled();
  Future<void>   setBiometricEnabled(bool enabled);
}

// Result type carrying outcome + lockout info for the UI.
class PinVerifyResult {
  final bool ok;
  final bool lockedOut;
  final Duration? retryAfter;
  final int remainingAttempts;
}
```

`BiometricService` is a separate seam wrapping `local_auth` (see §6):

```
abstract class BiometricService {

  Future<bool> isDeviceSupported();
  Future<bool> authenticate({required String reason});
}
```

## 3. Secure storage layout

Backend: `flutter_secure_storage` 9.2.2 with
```
AndroidOptions(encryptedSharedPreferences: true)
```
(AES-256, key material held in AndroidKeyStore — not extractable, survives backups correctly). Provide this via a single shared `AndroidOptions` getter so every instance is configured identically.

**Keys stored in secure storage:**

| Key | Type | Survives restart? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pin_salt` | base64 string | yes | salt for PBKDF2 |
| `pin_hash` | base64 string | yes | derived key |
| `pin_algo_version` | int-as-string | yes | migration hook |
| `pin_iterations` | int-as-string | yes | reproducible verify |
| `app_lock_enabled` | "true"/"false" | yes | master on/off for the feature |
| `biometric_enabled` | "true"/"false" | yes | user opted into fingerprint |
| `failed_attempts` | int-as-string | **yes (required)** | lockout must survive force-kill |
| `lockout_until` | epoch-millis string | **yes (required)** | lockout must survive force-kill |

**`last_background` timestamp → kept in MEMORY only (Riverpod state), NOT secure storage.** Rationale: cold start should *always* re-lock. A killed-and-restarted app having no timestamp → "locked" is the correct behavior. Persisting the timestamp would let a force-kill bypass the re-lock grace window. Only the failure counters need persistence.

**Why secure storage and not SharedPreferences for the secret:** the existing `theme_mode_provider.dart` uses plain `SharedPreferences`, which on Android is an unencrypted XML file in the app sandbox — readable on a rooted device or via `adb` backup. The PIN hash + salt + lockout counters are security-sensitive; they belong in Keystore-backed encrypted storage. Non-secret UI prefs can stay in SharedPreferences. (The `app_lock_enabled`/`biometric_enabled` flags are not strictly secret but live alongside the secret for a single coherent store.)

**Firestore constraint (one explicit line in the plan and in code comments):** none of the `pin_*`, lockout, or biometric fields ever touch `buildProfilePatch`, the `updateProfile` callable, or any Firestore doc. The secret is device-local only.

## 2. PIN cryptography design

**Honest framing (must appear in code docs):** a 4–6 digit PIN has only 10⁴–10⁶ entropy. PBKDF2 does **not** make it offline-brute-force-proof. The *primary* defenses are (a) Keystore-backed secure storage protecting the hash at rest, and (b) lockout/backoff limiting online guesses. PBKDF2 is defense-in-depth (slows an attacker who already extracted the hash). Do not describe SHA-256-or-PBKDF2 as "secure" without this context.

**Algorithm:** PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256.
- **Salt:** 16 bytes from a CSPRNG (`Random.secure()`), unique per PIN set.
- **Iterations:** `100000` in production; **injectable** so the unit suite can run with e.g. `1000` (100k × the test matrix would crawl).
- **Derived key length:** 32 bytes.
- **Stored fields** (all in secure storage, see §3):
  - `pin_salt` — base64 of the 16-byte salt
  - `pin_hash` — base64 of the 32-byte derived key
  - `pin_algo_version` — integer, currently `1` (lets a future migration re-hash transparently)
  - `pin_iterations` — integer (store the count actually used, so verify reproduces it even if the default changes)
- **Verify:** re-derive with stored salt + iterations, compare in **constant time** (fixed-length byte XOR-accumulate; never `==` on the strings, never early-return on first mismatch).
- **Salt uniqueness:** two consecutive `setPin` calls with the same PIN must yield different salts and different hashes (a unit test asserts this).

**Lockout / backoff:**
- Counter `failed_attempts` and `lockout_until` (epoch millis) live in **secure storage** so they survive an app restart — otherwise lockout is trivially bypassed by force-killing the app.
- Policy: after **5** consecutive failures, lock for a backoff window (e.g. 30s, then escalate: 30s → 1m → 5m). On a correct PIN, reset `failed_attempts` to 0 and clear `lockout_until`.
- `verifyPin` consults `lockout_until` first and returns a "locked-out, retry-after" result without even hashing when inside the window.

**`PinService` / `AppLockStore` API (signatures only — no implementation):**

```
// AppLockStore — thin async wrapper over the storage backend (the testable seam).
abstract class AppLockStore {
  Future<String?> read(String key);
  Future<void> write(String key, String value);
  Future<void> delete(String key);
  Future<void> deleteAll();
}

// PinService — pure-ish crypto + policy over an AppLockStore.
class PinService {
  PinService(this._store, {int iterations = 100000, Random? random});

  Future<bool>   hasPin();
  Future<void>   setPin(String pin);                 // generates salt, hashes, persists, resets counters
  Future<PinVerifyResult> verifyPin(String pin);     // checks lockout, hashes, constant-time compares, updates counters
  Future<void>   clearPin();                          // wipes pin_* + counters (used on disable / optional sign-out)

  Future<bool>   isAppLockEnabled();
  Future<void>   setAppLockEnabled(bool enabled);
  Future<bool>   isBiometricEnabled();
  Future<void>   setBiometricEnabled(bool enabled);
}

// Result type carrying outcome + lockout info for the UI.
class PinVerifyResult {
  final bool ok;
  final bool lockedOut;
  final Duration? retryAfter;
  final int remainingAttempts;
}
```

## 3. Secure storage layout

Backend: `flutter_secure_storage` 9.2.2 with
```
AndroidOptions(encryptedSharedPreferences: true)
```
(AES-256, key material held in AndroidKeyStore — not extractable, survives backups correctly). Provide this via a single shared `AndroidOptions` getter so every instance is configured identically.

**Keys stored in secure storage:**

| Key | Type | Survives restart? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pin_salt` | base64 string | yes | salt for PBKDF2 |
| `pin_hash` | base64 string | yes | derived key |
| `pin_algo_version` | int-as-string | yes | migration hook |
| `pin_iterations` | int-as-string | yes | reproducible verify |
| `app_lock_enabled` | "true"/"false" | yes | master on/off for the feature |
| `biometric_enabled` | "true"/"false" | yes | user opted into fingerprint |
| `failed_attempts` | int-as-string | **yes (required)** | lockout must survive force-kill |
| `lockout_until` | epoch-millis string | **yes (required)** | lockout must survive force-kill |

**`last_background` timestamp → kept in MEMORY only (Riverpod state), NOT secure storage.** Rationale: cold start should *always* re-lock. A killed-and-restarted app having no timestamp → "locked" is the correct behavior. Persisting the timestamp would let a force-kill bypass the re-lock grace window. Only the failure counters need persistence.

**Why secure storage and not SharedPreferences for the secret:** the existing `theme_mode_provider.dart` uses plain `SharedPreferences`, which on Android is an unencrypted XML file in the app sandbox — readable on a rooted device or via `adb` backup. The PIN hash + salt + lockout counters are security-sensitive; they belong in Keystore-backed encrypted storage. Non-secret UI prefs can stay in SharedPreferences. (The `app_lock_enabled`/`biometric_enabled` flags are not strictly secret but live alongside the secret for a single coherent store.)

**Firestore constraint (one explicit line in the plan and in code comments):** none of the `pin_*`, lockout, or biometric fields ever touch `buildProfilePatch`, the `updateProfile` callable, or any Firestore doc. The secret is device-local only.

# App-Lock: PIN + Fingerprint

## Context

The user wants to add a **PIN code** and **biometric fingerprint** lock to the DroneAid Flutter app. **It is feasible** — the codebase has a clean Riverpod + go_router auth layer and an existing settings page to extend.

The feature is a **device-local app-lock layered on top of** the existing Firebase login (Thai national-ID + password), **not** a replacement for it:

```
Login (ID+password) once  →  Firebase session persists
Open app → LOCKED → PIN or fingerprint → app content
Background → resume (>30s) → LOCKED again
```

Decisions confirmed with the user:
- **App-lock over login** (existing login untouched; the lock secret is device-local, never synced to Firestore).
- **Lock on cold start AND background-resume** past a 30s grace window (quick app-switches don't nag). A "Lock now" affordance is included.
- **Demoed on the Android emulator** (fingerprint simulated via `adb emu finger touch`).
- App-lock only engages when the user has **set a PIN** in settings; otherwise the app behaves exactly as today.

**Scope honesty:** today (2026-06-04) is the project deadline and this feature is **not** in the original milestone spec — no PIN/biometric/app-lock requirement exists in `docs/`. This is a deliberate post-spec addition (~7 new Dart files + Android native edits + tests; realistically multi-day, not a same-day land). Per ADR 0002 "done = full features on emulator," it fits the emulator-demo model, but it is net-new scope.

---

## Approach

**Gate = widget overlay**, *not* a go_router redirect. The existing `main.dart` `MaterialApp.router` `builder:` already renders `AuthSplash()` over the router while auth loads (`main.dart:92-96`). We extend that same proven seam with one more branch. `router.dart` and `auth_providers.dart` are **left untouched** — this avoids racing the existing auth redirect, preserves deep links for free (the real destination resolves underneath the overlay), and is role-agnostic.

Gate ordering (auth checked **before** lock, so the lock never appears over `/login`):

```dart
final auth = ref.watch(authStateProvider);
if (auth.isLoading) return const AuthSplash();
if (auth.valueOrNull == null) return child;          // signed out → router shows /login
final lock = ref.watch(appLockStateProvider);
if (lock.status == AppLockStatus.unknown) return const AuthSplash(); // hydrating
if (lock.status == AppLockStatus.locked) return const LockScreen();
return child;                                          // disabled or unlocked
```

Secrets stored **per-uid** in Keystore-backed `flutter_secure_storage`, so signing out and a different user signing in on the same device re-evaluates against the new uid's keys (closes the cross-user bypass).

---

## Packages (`app/pubspec.yaml`)

| Package | Constraint | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `local_auth` | `^2.3.0` | Fingerprint prompt. Requires `FlutterFragmentActivity` (below). |
| `flutter_secure_storage` | `9.2.2` (`^9.2.2`, stays `<10`) | Keystore-backed store. **Pin to 9.x:** 10.0.0 removed the `encryptedSharedPreferences` option. |
| `pointycastle` | `^3.9.1` | PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 for the PIN (pure-Dart, runs in `flutter test`). |

Do **not** add `crypto` — PointyCastle covers PBKDF2; constant-time compare is a short XOR loop.

---

## PIN cryptography

PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256: 16-byte CSPRNG salt (`Random.secure()`), **100000** iterations (injectable — tests use `1000`), 32-byte derived key, constant-time compare. Stored fields (all in secure storage, base64/int-as-string): `pin_salt`, `pin_hash`, `pin_iterations`, `pin_algo_version` (=1, migration hook).

**Lockout:** `failed_attempts` + `lockout_until` (epoch millis) **in secure storage** (must survive force-kill). After 5 failures → 30s cooldown (escalating). `verifyPin` checks `lockout_until` first and short-circuits without hashing while inside the window. Correct PIN resets the counter.

Code-comment honesty: a 4–6 digit PIN has low entropy; PBKDF2 + Keystore-at-rest + lockout are defense-in-depth, not brute-force-proof.

---

## Native Android (verified facts)

- **`MainActivity.kt`** (`android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/droneaid/droneaid/MainActivity.kt`) — change `FlutterActivity` → `FlutterFragmentActivity` (import + superclass). Required by `local_auth`; assessed safe — no existing plugin (firebase_*, geolocator, flutter_map) needs a plain `FlutterActivity`.
- **`AndroidManifest.xml`** — add `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.USE_BIOMETRIC"/>`.
- **`build.gradle.kts`** `defaultConfig` — set `minSdk = maxOf(23, flutter.minSdkVersion)`. Documented floor for BiometricPrompt + secure-storage; the installed Flutter already resolves `flutter.minSdkVersion = 24`, so this is documentation, not a forced bump.

---

## Files

### Create — Dart
- `app/lib/core/applock/app_lock_store.dart` — `AppLockStore` interface + `SecureAppLockStore` (flutter_secure_storage 9.x, `AndroidOptions(encryptedSharedPreferences: true)`) + key constants. (`applock` namespace avoids colliding with the unrelated map `pin_picker`/`DeliveryPin` and the admin-side `UserProfile.locked` field.)
- `app/lib/core/applock/pin_service.dart` — PBKDF2 hash/verify, salt gen, constant-time compare, lockout policy, `PinVerifyResult{ok, lockedOut, retryAfter, remainingAttempts}`. Constructor takes `{int iterations, Random? random, DateTime Function() now}` — **`now` injectable** for lockout/grace tests.
- `app/lib/core/applock/biometric_service.dart` — `BiometricService` interface + `LocalAuthBiometricService`. `authenticate` uses `AuthenticationOptions(biometricOnly: true, stickyAuth: true)` — **`biometricOnly: true`** so the OS does **not** offer the device credential (which would bypass our app PIN + lockout); biometric cancel/fail falls back to our keypad.
- `app/lib/core/applock/app_lock_providers.dart` — `pinServiceProvider`, `biometricServiceProvider`, and `appLockStateProvider` (`StateNotifier<AppLockState>` holding `status ∈ {unknown, disabled, locked, unlocked}` + in-memory `backgroundedAt`). Hydrates on construct; `ref.listen(authStateProvider)` re-hydrates per-uid and sets `disabled` on sign-out.
- `app/lib/core/applock/app_lock_gate.dart` — owns the **`AppLifecycleListener`**: `onPause/onHide` records `backgroundedAt = now()`; `onResume` re-locks if enabled & unlocked & elapsed ≥ 30s (no timestamp → lock defensively). Instantiated app-wide via one `ref.watch(appLockStateProvider)` line in `DroneAidApp.build` (alongside the existing `fcmRegistrationProvider`/`devTickRunnerProvider` watches).
- `app/lib/features/applock/lock_screen.dart` — full-screen `Scaffold` in `PopScope(canPop: false)`. `PinKeypad` (dots + 3×4 grid + backspace), "Use fingerprint" action (shown only when biometric enabled **and** `canCheckBiometrics`), error/cooldown messaging via `colorScheme.error`, design tokens from `tokens.dart`, `BrandMark` logo. **"Forgot PIN? Sign out"** escape hatch → `authRepository.signOut()` + `clearPin(uid)` → status `disabled` → router shows `/login` (the only way out of a forgotten lock, since `profile_page.dart` is behind the gate). Auto-trigger biometric once on mount, guarded by a `_prompted` flag so it doesn't re-fire on rebuild/cancel.
- `app/lib/features/applock/pin_keypad.dart` — reusable numeric keypad widget (used by lock screen + set-PIN flow).
- `app/lib/features/applock/set_pin_page.dart` — set / confirm / change PIN flow (reuses `PinKeypad` in a modal).

### Modify — Dart
- `app/lib/main.dart` — extend `MaterialApp.router` `builder:` with the gate ordering above; add `ref.watch(appLockStateProvider)` in `DroneAidApp.build`.
- `app/lib/features/user/profile_page.dart` — add a `_SectionCard(title: 'Security')` after "Preferences": App-lock switch (set-PIN flow when on, `clearPin` when off), Change PIN, Enable-fingerprint `SwitchListTile` (disabled unless PIN set **and** device-capable). **Wired straight to the providers — never through `buildProfilePatch`/`updateProfile`/Firestore.** Security section is user-only (profile page lives in the user shell; admins have no PIN — acceptable for the demo).

### Modify — Android native
- `app/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/droneaid/droneaid/MainActivity.kt` — `FlutterFragmentActivity`.
- `app/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` — `USE_BIOMETRIC`.
- `app/android/app/build.gradle.kts` — `minSdk = maxOf(23, flutter.minSdkVersion)`.

### Create — tests (`flutter test`; fakes behind interfaces, Riverpod `overrideWith` per repo convention)
- `app/test/core/applock/in_memory_app_lock_store.dart` — `Map`-backed fake `AppLockStore`.
- `app/test/core/applock/fake_biometric_service.dart` — scripted `BiometricService`.
- `app/test/core/applock/pin_service_test.dart` — set→verify ok; wrong PIN; 5-fail lockout + survives "restart" (fresh service over same map); salt uniqueness; `clearPin`; iteration round-trip.
- `app/test/core/applock/app_lock_state_test.dart` — **grace-window math via injected clock**: unlocked→bg@T→resume@T+10s stays unlocked; resume@T+31s → locked; cold start (no timestamp) → locked.
- `app/test/features/applock/lock_screen_test.dart` — correct PIN unlocks; wrong PIN errors + stays; lockout message after N; fingerprint button visibility + fake success/fail→PIN fallback; "Forgot PIN" calls signOut+clearPin.
- `app/test/features/user/profile_security_section_test.dart` — section renders; toggle on→set-PIN flow, off→`clearPin`; fingerprint toggle disabled when `canCheckBiometrics==false`; assert **no** PIN field appears in `buildProfilePatch` output (guards the Firestore-exclusion constraint).

---

## Edge cases handled

- **Forgot PIN** → "Sign out" escape on lock screen (clears PIN for that uid). Normal logout *retains* the PIN (per-uid); only the forgot-escape clears it — deliberate asymmetry.
- **Cold start** always locks (no timestamp); 30s grace applies only to resume.
- **Sign-out / user-switch** → `authStateProvider` listener re-hydrates per-uid; user B isn't gated by user A's PIN.
- **No PIN set** → `disabled` → app behaves exactly as today.
- **Hot restart** → re-hydrates → re-locks (mimics cold start).

---

## Verification

1. **Unit/widget tests:** `cd app && flutter test` — all new suites green (pure-Dart; no emulator needed).
2. **Static:** `flutter analyze` clean (CI has a strict-lint gate).
3. **Build:** `flutter pub get` resolves; `flutter build apk --debug` succeeds (confirms FragmentActivity + manifest + minSdk edits compile).
4. **Manual on emulator** (full stack via `bun scripts/dev.ts`):
   - Log in (demo user `[REDACTED:thai-id]`) → set a PIN in Settings → Security.
   - Hot-restart (`R`) → lock screen appears → wrong PIN errors, correct PIN unlocks.
   - Background the app, wait >30s, resume → re-locked.
   - Enroll a fingerprint on the emulator (Settings → Security → add fingerprint, completing enrollment with `adb -e emu finger touch 1`). Enable fingerprint in app Settings → lock → tap "Use fingerprint" → `adb -e emu finger touch 1` → unlocks.
   - "Forgot PIN? Sign out" → returns to `/login`.
   - Verify a user who never sets a PIN sees no lock screen (no regression).

- `app/lib/core/applock/biometric_service.dart` — `BiometricService` interface + `LocalAuthBiometricService`. `authenticate` uses `AuthenticationOptions(biometricOnly: true, stickyAuth: true)` — **`biometricOnly: true`** so the OS does **not** offer the device credential (which would bypass our app PIN + lockout); biometric cancel/fail falls back to our keypad.
- `app/lib/core/applock/app_lock_providers.dart` — `pinServiceProvider`, `biometricServiceProvider`, and `appLockStateProvider` (`StateNotifier<AppLockState>` holding `status ∈ {unknown, disabled, locked, unlocked}` + in-memory `backgroundedAt`). Hydrates on construct; `ref.listen(authStateProvider)` re-hydrates per-uid and sets `disabled` on sign-out.
- `app/lib/core/applock/app_lock_gate.dart` — owns the **`AppLifecycleListener`**: `onPause/onHide` records `backgroundedAt = now()`; `onResume` re-locks if enabled & unlocked & elapsed ≥ 30s (no timestamp → lock defensively). Instantiated app-wide via one `ref.watch(appLockStateProvider)` line in `DroneAidApp.build` (alongside the existing `fcmRegistrationProvider`/`devTickRunnerProvider` watches).
- `app/lib/features/applock/lock_screen.dart` — full-screen `Scaffold` in `PopScope(canPop: false)`. `PinKeypad` (dots + 3×4 grid + backspace), "Use fingerprint" action (shown only when biometric enabled **and** `canCheckBiometrics`), error/cooldown messaging via `colorScheme.error`, design tokens from `tokens.dart`, `BrandMark` logo. **"Forgot PIN? Sign out"** escape hatch → `authRepository.signOut()` + `clearPin(uid)` → status `disabled` → router shows `/login` (the only way out of a forgotten lock, since `profile_page.dart` is behind the gate). Auto-trigger biometric once on mount, guarded by a `_prompted` flag so it doesn't re-fire on rebuild/cancel.
- `app/lib/features/applock/pin_keypad.dart` — reusable numeric keypad widget (used by lock screen + set-PIN flow).
- `app/lib/features/applock/set_pin_page.dart` — set / confirm / change PIN flow (reuses `PinKeypad` in a modal).

### Modify — Dart
- `app/lib/main.dart` — extend `MaterialApp.router` `builder:` with the gate ordering above; add `ref.watch(appLockStateProvider)` in `DroneAidApp.build`.
- `app/lib/features/user/profile_page.dart` — add a `_SectionCard(title: 'Security')` after "Preferences": App-lock switch (set-PIN flow when on, `clearPin` when off), Change PIN, Enable-fingerprint `SwitchListTile` (disabled unless PIN set **and** device-capable). **Wired straight to the providers — never through `buildProfilePatch`/`updateProfile`/Firestore.** Security section is user-only (profile page lives in the user shell; admins have no PIN — acceptable for the demo).

### Modify — Android native
- `app/android/app/src/main/kotlin/com/droneaid/droneaid/MainActivity.kt` — `FlutterFragmentActivity`.
- `app/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` — `USE_BIOMETRIC`.
- `app/android/app/build.gradle.kts` — `minSdk = maxOf(23, flutter.minSdkVersion)`.

### Create — tests (`flutter test`; fakes behind interfaces, Riverpod `overrideWith` per repo convention)
- `app/test/core/applock/in_memory_app_lock_store.dart` — `Map`-backed fake `AppLockStore`.
- `app/test/core/applock/fake_biometric_service.dart` — scripted `BiometricService`.
- `app/test/core/applock/pin_service_test.dart` — set→verify ok; wrong PIN; 5-fail lockout + survives "restart" (fresh service over same map); salt uniqueness; `clearPin`; iteration round-trip.
- `app/test/core/applock/app_lock_state_test.dart` — **grace-window math via injected clock**: unlocked→bg@T→resume@T+10s stays unlocked; resume@T+31s → locked; cold start (no timestamp) → locked.
- `app/test/features/applock/lock_screen_test.dart` — correct PIN unlocks; wrong PIN errors + stays; lockout message after N; fingerprint button visibility + fake success/fail→PIN fallback; "Forgot PIN" calls signOut+clearPin.
- `app/test/features/user/profile_security_section_test.dart` — section renders; toggle on→set-PIN flow, off→`clearPin`; fingerprint toggle disabled when `canCheckBiometrics==false`; assert **no** PIN field appears in `buildProfilePatch` output (guards the Firestore-exclusion constraint).

---

## Edge cases handled

- **Forgot PIN** → "Sign out" escape on lock screen (clears PIN for that uid). Normal logout *retains* the PIN (per-uid); only the forgot-escape clears it — deliberate asymmetry.
- **Cold start** always locks (no timestamp); 30s grace applies only to resume.
- **Sign-out / user-switch** → `authStateProvider` listener re-hydrates per-uid; user B isn't gated by user A's PIN.
- **No PIN set** → `disabled` → app behaves exactly as today.
- **Hot restart** → re-hydrates → re-locks (mimics cold start).

---

## Verification

1. **Unit/widget tests:** `cd app && flutter test` — all new suites green (pure-Dart; no emulator needed).
2. **Static:** `flutter analyze` clean (CI has a strict-lint gate).
3. **Build:** `flutter pub get` resolves; `flutter build apk --debug` succeeds (confirms FragmentActivity + manifest + minSdk edits compile).
4. **Manual on emulator** (full stack via `bun scripts/dev.ts`):
   - Log in (demo user `[REDACTED:thai-id]`) → set a PIN in Settings → Security.
   - Hot-restart (`R`) → lock screen appears → wrong PIN errors, correct PIN unlocks.
   - Background the app, wait >30s, resume → re-locked.
   - Enroll a fingerprint on the emulator (Settings → Security → add fingerprint, completing enrollment with `adb -e emu finger touch 1`). Enable fingerprint in app Settings → lock → tap "Use fingerprint" → `adb -e emu finger touch 1` → unlocks.
   - "Forgot PIN? Sign out" → returns to `/login`.
   - Verify a user who never sets a PIN sees no lock screen (no regression).

Two unrelated "lock" concepts exist — do not conflate them:

- **`UserProfile.locked`** (`app/lib/core/auth/user_profile.dart`) is the **server-side admin account lock** (spec F-AUTH-05: "Admin can lock/unlock a user account"). It lives in Firestore `users/{uid}`.
- **App-lock** (`app/lib/core/applock/`) is a **device-local PIN + fingerprint** gate layered over Firebase login, added 2026-06-04. Its secret is stored per-uid in Keystore-backed `flutter_secure_storage` and **never** touches Firestore.

App-lock design: gate is a widget overlay in `main.dart`'s `MaterialApp.router` builder (not a go_router redirect); `AppLockController` (in `app_lock_providers.dart`) owns the lifecycle listener and re-locks on background→resume past a 30s grace window. PIN = PBKDF2 (pointycastle). `MainActivity` extends `FlutterFragmentActivity` (required by local_auth). Settings live in the profile page "Security" section, user-only.

**Why:** a future change touching "locked" could wrongly assume one means the other. **How to apply:** for app-open security use the applock layer; for admin disabling an account use `UserProfile.locked`.

APK built clean (197M debug) — `FlutterFragmentActivity` + the 3 new plugins compile. Warnings are pre-existing (KGP deprecation on `cloud_functions`/`shared_preferences`, not my code).

Full verification green. Calling advisor before declaring done.

One real blocker, and it's exactly in the seam your green checks can't see. `flutter analyze` + 202 tests + APK build are real, but every test overrides `appLockControllerProvider` with an already-hydrated controller and never overrides `authStateProvider` — so the actual gate wiring in `main.dart` (the `ref.listen(authStateProvider, …, fireImmediately: true)` + async hydrate) runs in zero tests.

**The bug: content flashes before the lock screen on cold start, for PIN users specifically.**

Trace cold-start with a logged-in user who has a PIN:
1. `authStateProvider` starts `AsyncLoading`. `fireImmediately` fires the listener with `next.valueOrNull?.uid == null` → `onUserChanged(null)` → **status = disabled.** Your carefully-designed `unknown` initial state is overwritten before it ever does its job.
2. Auth resolves to the real `User`. Listener fires `onUserChanged(uid)` → `_uid = uid` → `await _hydrate()`. Hydrate awaits **real method channels** (`flutter_secure_storage.read`, `local_auth.isAvailable`) — multiple frames.
3. During that await window, status is still `disabled`. The builder reruns (auth changed), hits `auth not loading && user != null && status == disabled` → **returns `child`** → home page paints.
4. Hydrate completes → `locked` → builder reruns → `LockScreen`.

So the authenticated content is visible for the duration of two plugin round-trips before the lock appears. That defeats the feature's whole point, and it lands precisely on PIN-enabled users (no-PIN users correctly resolve to `disabled`, no flash). A grader cold-starting the locked app hits it on attempt one.

**This blocks.** It's not cosmetic — it's the security path.

**Fix** — don't let a *loading* auth state collapse to `disabled`. Guard the listener:
```dart
(_, next) {
  if (next.isLoading) return;        // stay 'unknown' → builder shows AuthSplash, never child
  controller.onUserChanged(next.valueOrNull?.uid);
}
```
With this, status stays `unknown` through loading and through the hydrate window → builder shows `AuthSplash`, never content, until `locked`/`disabled` is known. (Cost: no-PIN users see a brief splash instead of instant home while storage is read — correct and negligible.)

**Make it testable** (this is why the bug escaped): the decision lives in the listener, which no test exercises, and faking a Firebase `User` for an `authStateProvider` override is painful. Extract the mapping into a controller method so it needs no fake `User`:
```dart
void onAuthState({required bool isLoading, required String? uid}) {
  if (isLoading) return;
  onUserChanged(uid);
}
```
Then a pure unit test asserts the ordering: seed a PIN in the in-memory store, call `onAuthState(isLoading: true, uid: null)` → expect `unknown` (not `disabled`); then `onAuthState(isLoading: false, uid: 'u1')` and await → expect it goes `unknown → locked`, never passing through `disabled`. That's the regression guard for the exact path that's currently dark.

Verify the real thing too if you get an emulator: cold-start with a PIN set, watch for the home-screen flash before the lock.

Everything else holds — don't touch the overlay-gate design (it's right), the PBKDF2/lockout logic (well-tested), or the native edits (APK proves they compile). Fix this one wiring guard, add the unit test, then you're done.

Advisor caught a real security bug the tests can't see: on cold start, the `fireImmediately` listener fires during `AsyncLoading` with `uid==null` → status collapses to `disabled`; then auth resolves and `_hydrate()` awaits real plugin reads — during that window the builder paints **content** before flipping to `locked`. Content flashes before the lock, specifically for PIN users. Fixing the wiring guard + adding the regression test for that exact path.

content.text:
Right — that's your emulator config, not mine to change. Reverting that intent. Here's the diagnosis + the commands for you to run.

**Not a code bug.** APK builds fine. The `Medium_Phone` AVD has a **6 GB data partition that's full** (Play Store system image fills most of it). The 131 MB debug APK won't fit. Host disk has 340 GB free — irrelevant; this is the emulator's internal `/data`.

**Fix — pick one (emulator must be stopped first; it already shut down):**

**A. Quick — wipe `/data` (frees the full partition, keeps 6 GB):**
```
emulator -avd Medium_Phone -wipe-data
```
Fresh `/data` has room for the APK. Wipes installed apps + their data (fine for dev).

**B. Better — more headroom (edit then wipe):**
Edit `~/.config/.android/avd/Medium_Phone.avd/config.ini`, change:
```
disk.dataPartition.size=6G   →   disk.dataPartition.size=12G
```
then cold-boot with wipe (resize only applies on wipe):
```
emulator -avd Medium_Phone -wipe-data
```
Or do both via GUI: Android Studio → Device Manager → `Medium_Phone` → edit → **Internal Storage = 12 GB**, then **Wipe Data**.

After either, re-run:
```
bun scripts/dev.ts
```

If `emulator` isn't on PATH, it's at `$ANDROID_SDK_ROOT/emulator/emulator` (or `~/Android/Sdk/emulator/emulator`).

Want me to run option A for you? Type `! emulator -avd Medium_Phone -wipe-data` to run it in-session, or say the word and I'll execute it.

=== log-presence job full ===
  log-presence:
    name: Agent log presence
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'
      - name: Check that PR author has a session log for the latest commit date
        env:
          PR_AUTHOR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import os, re, subprocess, sys
          from pathlib import Path

          author = os.environ.get("PR_AUTHOR", "")
          base = os.environ.get("BASE_SHA", "")
          head = os.environ.get("HEAD_SHA", "")

          # Resolve GitHub handle → folder name via docs/agent-logs/README.md table.
          mapping = {}
          for line in open("docs/agent-logs/README.md", encoding="utf-8"):
              m = re.match(r"\|\s*\w+\s*\|\s*`?(\w+)`?\s*\|\s*@?([\w-]+)\s*\|", line)
              if m:
                  mapping[m.group(2).lower()] = m.group(1).lower()

          folder = mapping.get(author.lower())
          if not folder:
              print(f"::warning::No agent-logs folder mapped to @{author}. Skipping log-presence check.")
              sys.exit(0)

          diff = subprocess.check_output(
              ["git", "diff", "--name-only", base, head], text=True,
          ).splitlines()
          touched_source = [
              p for p in diff
              if not p.startswith("docs/")
              and not p.startswith(".github/")
              and not p.startswith(".claude/")
              and p
          ]
          if not touched_source:
              print("log-presence OK (no source files touched).")
              sys.exit(0)

          # Relaxed rule: require a log file whose YYYY-MM-DD prefix matches the
          # latest commit's author date. A single log can satisfy multiple PRs
          # cut from the same day (e.g. small follow-ups), so we no longer
          # require the log to appear in this PR's diff.
          commit_date = subprocess.check_output(
              ["git", "show", "-s", "--format=%ad", "--date=format:%Y-%m-%d", head],
              text=True,
          ).strip()

          folder_path = Path(f"docs/agent-logs/{folder}")
          if not folder_path.is_dir():
              print(f"::error::No log folder at {folder_path} for @{author}.")
              sys.exit(1)

          today_logs = sorted(
              p.name for p in folder_path.glob("*.jsonl")
              if p.name.startswith(commit_date)
          )

          if not today_logs:
              print(f"::error::PR touches source files but @{author} has no docs/agent-logs/{folder}/{commit_date}_*.jsonl session log.")
              print(f"Latest commit ({head[:7]}) authored {commit_date}; expected at least one log file with that date prefix.")
              print("Touched:")
              for p in touched_source:
                  print(f"  {p}")
              print("To fix: run scripts/copy-claude-session.sh (or wait for the SessionEnd hook) and commit the resulting .jsonl on this branch.")
              sys.exit(1)

# DroneAid — Claude Code Agent Logs

Per the professor's requirement (and design spec §13), every team member's Claude Code session JSONL is committed to this folder so the work is auditable.

## Folder layout

```
docs/agent-logs/
├── README.md            (this file)
├── _index.md            generated locally by scripts/build-log-index.py (gitignored)
├── aok/                 Aok (Lead)
├── belle/               Belle
├── bew/                 Bew
├── poom/                Poom
├── tawan/               Tawan
```

Each per-dev folder receives that dev's session JSONL files, named `YYYY-MM-DD_<sessionId>_HHMMSS.jsonl`. The `HHMMSS` snapshot suffix means every flush writes a new file, so two branches can each carry the same Claude session id without colliding at merge time. Old snapshots are strict subsets of newer ones (Claude appends within a session) — keep them all.

## Handle table

| Real name | Folder name | GitHub handle |
|---|---|---|
| Aok | `aok` | @AokDesu |
| Belle | `belle` | @BBelleysp |
| Bew | `bew` | @SNOWxSAUSAGES |
| Poom | `poom` | @Mrmo0p |
| Tawan | `tawan` | @Tantawan7 |

When real GitHub handles are known, update this table and `.github/CODEOWNERS`.

## One-time setup per developer

1. Clone the repo to your machine.
2. Set the env var `DRONE_AID_HANDLE` to your folder name above.
   - Windows (persistent): `setx DRONE_AID_HANDLE aok`
   - macOS / Linux: add `export DRONE_AID_HANDLE=aok` to `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`.
3. Add a `SessionEnd` hook to your **personal** Claude Code settings file
   (`~/.claude/settings.json` on macOS/Linux; `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json` on Windows). Replace the path with **your own clone path**.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# DroneAid — Claude Code SessionEnd hook (POSIX shell).
#
# Copies the most-recently-modified Claude Code session JSONL for THIS project
# into docs/agent-logs/<your-handle>/, redacted of secrets via redact-secrets.py.
#
# Setup:
#   1. export DRONE_AID_HANDLE=aok        # one of: aok belle bew poom tawan
